topics.label: The Solar System in Depth
facts: The Solar System formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a cloud of gas and dust.
The Sun holds more than 99 percent of all the mass in the Solar System.
Saturn is famous for its wide, bright rings made of ice and rock.
Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun, and it is a cold, windy world.

questions.q: About how old is the Solar System?
questions.fact: The Solar System formed from a collapsing cloud of gas and dust about 4.6 billion years ago.

questions.q: How much of the Solar System's mass is in the Sun?
questions.fact: The Sun is so massive that it holds over 99 percent of the Solar System's mass.

questions.q: Which planet is famous for its wide, bright rings?
questions.fact: Saturn's rings are made of billions of pieces of ice and rock.

questions.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.fact: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun.

topics.label: Galaxies
facts: A galaxy is a huge group of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity.
Our galaxy is called the Milky Way, and it holds hundreds of billions of stars.
The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy, shaped like a giant spinning pinwheel.
Light from the nearest galaxy beyond our own takes about 2.5 million years to reach us.

choices: A huge group of stars, gas, and dust held together by gravity
questions.fact: Galaxies are enormous star systems, and there are billions of them in the universe.
We live in the Milky Way galaxy, which you can see as a milky band across a dark night sky.

questions.q: What shape is the Milky Way?
questions.fact: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy with arms curving out from its centre.

questions.q: How long does light from the nearest big galaxy take to reach us?
questions.fact: The Andromeda Galaxy is so far away that its light takes 2.5 million years to reach Earth.

topics.label: Black Holes
facts: A black hole is a place in space where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.
Black holes form when very massive stars run out of fuel and collapse.
The edge of a black hole is called the event horizon, and nothing that crosses it can come back.
Scientists have photographed the shadow of a black hole, and a giant one sits at the centre of our galaxy.

choices: A place where gravity is so strong not even light can escape
questions.fact: A black hole's gravity is so strong that light itself cannot escape from it.
When a huge star runs out of fuel, its core collapses under its own gravity.

questions.q: What is the edge of a black hole called?
questions.fact: The event horizon is the point of no return around a black hole.

questions.q: What sits at the centre of our Milky Way galaxy?
questions.fact: A black hole millions of times heavier than the Sun sits at the Milky Way's centre.

topics.label: The Universe
facts: The universe is everything that exists: all space, all stars, all galaxies, and all matter and energy.
Scientists think the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago with an event called the Big Bang.
The universe is still expanding, and galaxies are moving farther apart from each other.
A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 trillion kilometres.

choices: Everything that exists: all space, stars, galaxies, matter, and energy
questions.fact: The universe includes everything that exists.

questions.q: About how old is the universe?
questions.fact: Scientists estimate the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago.

questions.q: What is the universe doing now?
questions.fact: The universe is still expanding, with galaxies moving farther apart.

choices: The distance light travels in one year
The time it takes light to reach the Moon
